Current API throughput forces us to chunk into 50-card batches with manual delay between chunks or we get rate-limited. We built our own queuing system just to work around this.

title: - **Role:** Product Manager, Digital Banking Division - **Demographics:** 34, La
description:
- **Role:** Product Manager, Digital Banking Division
- **Demographics:** 34, Lagos, 8 years in banking product roles, manages a team responsible for a neobank's card products
- **Goals:** Launch card-based campaigns fast, keep integration overhead low, avoid engineering escalations reaching her desk
- **Frustrations:** Feature requests to Interswitch take multiple cycles to be scoped; no visibility into API roadmap; limit changes require full card reissuance
- **Behaviors:** Reviews API changelogs monthly, escalates to account manager when a workaround costs her team more than two engineering days
- **Needs:** Predictable roadmap communication, ability to adjust card controls without reissuance, clear SLAs for feature requests
- **Quote:** "I don't need more features. I need to stop being the translator between my engineers and your support team."
- **Jobs to be Done:** When rolling out a new card-based product, I want to configure and adjust card behavior without engineering rework, so I can hit launch dates without escalation.

description:
- **Role:** Operations Lead, Card Services
- **Demographics:** 41, Lagos, background in retail banking operations, oversees day-to-day card issue/block/dispute handling
- **Goals:** Resolve fraud and dispute cases quickly, minimize customer complaint escalations to his desk
- **Frustrations:** Delay between freeze confirmation and scheme-level enforcement; disputes where the timeline doesn't match what the dashboard shows
- **Behaviors:** Monitors the ops dashboard multiple times a day, personally handles high-severity fraud escalations

- **Quote:** "When I tell a customer their card is frozen, it needs to actually be frozen. Right now I'm not always telling the truth."
- **Jobs to be Done:** When fraud is reported, I want the freeze to take effect instantly and verifiably, so I can protect the customer and defend the bank's position in a dispute.

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Walk me through the last time you issued a ba
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Walk me through the last time you issued a batch of virtual cards for a campaign.
>
> **Interviewee:** We had a BNPL promo, needed 2,000 cards live in under 10 minutes for a flash campaign tied to a marketing push. We hit rate limits almost immediately when we tried to push all 2,000 through at once.
>
> **Interviewer:** What did you do?
>
> **Interviewee:** We had to build our own internal queue that chunks requests into batches of 50 with a delay between each chunk. It works, but it's fragile — if the delay is too short we get throttled, too long and we miss the campaign window.
>
> **Interviewer:** How often does this come up?
>
> **Interviewee:** Every major campaign. At least once a month. It's become expected overhead in our planning now, which honestly shouldn't be normal.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to be a problem?
>
> **Interviewee:** An async batch endpoint. We submit the whole batch, get a job ID, and get notified when it's done. We don't need synchronous responses for 2,000 cards — we need reliability and a completion signal.

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Walk me through what happens when a card gets
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Walk me through what happens when a card gets blocked or frozen.
>
> **Interviewee:** Customer calls in reporting suspected fraud. We hit the freeze endpoint, get a 200 success response, dashboard shows "frozen." We tell the customer they're protected.
>
> **Interviewer:** And then?
>
> **Interviewee:** Sometimes a transaction still goes through in the next few minutes. We've had two disputes where the customer swears they saw a charge after we told them it was frozen — and they're right, it did happen, because the scheme hadn't caught up yet.
>
> **Interviewer:** How did that make your team feel?
>
> **Interviewee:** Exposed. We're telling customers something is true based on what your API tells us, and it turns out that's not always the real-time truth. That's a liability problem for us, not just an inconvenience.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to happen?
>
> **Interviewee:** I need confirmation that the freeze is actually live at the scheme level before I tell my dashboard — and my customer — that it's done.

title: **Transcript:** > **Interviewer:** Think of the most painful part of your curren
description:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Think of the most painful part of your current workflow. Can you describe a specific moment when that pain showed up?
>
> **Interviewee:** Every CBN audit cycle. I need issuance and status logs for a specific date range. There's no self-serve way to get that — I open a support ticket and wait.
>
> **Interviewer:** How long does that usually take?
>
> **Interviewee:** Anywhere from two to five business days, depending on how backed up support is. If the audit deadline is tight, that's genuinely stressful.
>
> **Interviewer:** What do you do to work around it?
>
> **Interviewee:** I keep my own shadow spreadsheet, updated manually, so I'm not fully dependent on their turnaround. It's extra work I shouldn't have to do.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to be a problem?
>
> **Interviewee:** A dashboard where I filter by date range and export the log myself. I don't need anything fancy. I need independence from the ticket queue.

title: - **Hypothesis:** If banks can submit card issuance as an async batch job instea
description:
- **Hypothesis:** If banks can submit card issuance as an async batch job instead of chunked synchronous calls, campaign-related engineering escalations will drop by at least 30%.
- **Success Metric:** ≥30% reduction in campaign-related engineering escalations among pilot banks over two campaign cycles.
- **Failure Metric:** No measurable reduction, or job completion time exceeds current chunked-call throughput.
- **Duration:** 8 weeks (covering two campaign cycles)
- **Cost:** High — requires new async job infrastructure and status tracking
- **Risk:** Medium — job queue reliability under peak load is untested
- **Expected Learning:** Whether async issuance removes the need for customer-side workaround queues, and what batch size/throughput ceiling is realistic.
- **Results:** Pending — pilot scheduled for next quarter, not yet run.

title: - **Hypothesis:** If compliance officers can self-serve export issuance/status l
description:
- **Hypothesis:** If compliance officers can self-serve export issuance/status logs by date range, dependency on support tickets for audit prep will drop to near zero.
- **Success Metric:** ≥90% of audit-related log requests handled via self-serve export within one quarter of launch, with zero related support tickets.
- **Failure Metric:** <50% adoption, or continued reliance on manual ticket-based requests.
- **Duration:** 4 weeks (prototype walkthrough, not full build)
- **Cost:** Low — clickable prototype only, no backend build
- **Risk:** Low
- **Expected Learning:** Whether the proposed export/filter UX matches how compliance officers actually structure audit requests, before committing engineering resources.
- **Results:** Prototype walkthrough with 3 compliance officers across 3 customers — all 3 completed the export flow without assistance and confirmed the filter fields matched their audit format. Hypothesis supported — recommend moving to build.

title: | Assumption Statement | Evidence | |------------------------|----------| | Poll
description:
| Assumption Statement | Evidence |
|------------------------|----------|
| Polling for card status is a significant source of downstream support burden for fintechs. | 3 out of 5 interviewees mentioned this unprompted |
| Delayed scheme-level freeze enforcement creates real dispute/liability exposure for banks, not just inconvenience. | 2 out of 5 interviewees described a specific dispute case caused by this |
| Compliance officers will adopt a self-serve export tool if it matches their existing audit data format. | 3 out of 3 compliance interviewees confirmed this in prototype testing |
| Banks running card-based campaigns build their own workaround infrastructure to compensate for API throughput limits. | 4 out of 5 interviewees confirmed building internal queuing/chunking logic |
| Ambiguous error codes cause engineering teams to file support tickets rather than self-diagnose. | 21 support tickets over 90 days traced to generic error responses (CMP-06) |
| Sandbox instability actively erodes trust in using sandbox beyond basic smoke testing. | 2 out of 5 interviewees stated they no longer trust sandbox for regression testing |
| Post-issuance limit/control changes are a recurring ask but not an urgent blocker for most bank product teams. | Mentioned in 4 of 6 renewal calls (CMP-07), but not raised unprompted in story-based interviews |
